architecture.mechanism: Absorbing heat during the melting of phase-change materials
architecture.intervention: Integrate a thin layer of high-latent-heat composite phase-change material between battery cells in the e-bike pack to absorb thermal energy passively during long climbs without adding active cooling hardware.
architecture.expected_effect: Cell temperatures remain below 50C during sustained high-load climbing by absorbing excess heat as latent heat of fusion, preventing BMS cutoff at 60C while adding minimal weight compared to active liquid cooling systems.
architecture.falsification_test: Instrument the battery pack with thermocouples and perform a standardized climb simulation on a dynamometer; if peak cell temperature exceeds 50C or total added pack mass exceeds 5% of original pack mass, the intervention fails.
